plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling fields of slender silver-green stems topped with fragrant violet-blue flower spikes hum with bees and perfume the warm summer air. Lavender in full bloom is one of Provence's best-known sights.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, usually peaking in July in southern France
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, cup-shaped blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, waxy leaves that float on warm, still ponds. Each flower opens at dawn and closes again by afternoon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, roughly June through September in temperate East Asia, with peak bloom in July and August
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across East Asia, including China and Japan
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic texture that makes water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt with it. Engineers call this the 'lotus effect' and copy it in self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rose-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. They are a staple of summer prairies and cottage gardens, and butterflies and goldfinches visit them constantly.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer through early fall, with peak bloom in July and August
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, including the prairies of the United States Midwest
plants.funFact: The 'cone' is a dome of tiny individual flowers. The name Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, a reference to its spiny center.
